estimate.definition: 20 log10(V(f_res) L / (1 V * 1 mm)): f_res the half-wave resonance c / (2 L sqrt(eps_eff)) of the gap's slot, L the slot length perpendicular to the crossing in mm, V the continuous-bound amplitude (volts, single-sided peak) of the signal's spectrum at f_res for its swing and its shorter edge. The headline uses the continuous bound because it is the one of the three spectrum quantities that needs no assumption about the data pattern; the named pattern lines and random data in a resolution bandwidth are carried beside it, each with its own score. Not a field, no distance, no limit: it ranks the slots of one board against each other
estimate.method: ranking score of the worst gap: slot 76.000 mm, half-wave resonance 1123.0 MHz, continuous-bound amplitude 0.2546 V of a 0.400 V swing with a 0.125 ns ramp
not_modelled: whether a cut that reaches the plane edge is a notch open at one end, which resonates at a quarter wave (half the frequency the score uses; carried as quarter_wave_resonance_hz), or a cut through the plane
slot radiation efficiency (how much of the power a slot of this length takes up and radiates depends on how it is fed, its width and the structure around it)
plane-pair cavity modes (a pair of planes resonates as a cavity; a slot, a cut or a row of vias only perturbs it)
enclosure, chassis and cable coupling (the field outside the board, and what the slot's voltage drives)
the common-mode part of a differential pair: the score uses the whole signal, a balanced pair excites a slot only through the part that is converted (mode conversion is a later check)
return current outside the coverage window, current crowding at a slot's ends and the inductance of the detour
the plane of a stripline other than the nearer one, and a reference net that changes inside one plane layer

inputs_text: reference window: return current taken within 3 H each side of a trace (79.5 % of a thin trace's return current over an infinite plane; derived, band 2 H to 5 H)
edge distance: plane and board edges kept 20 H from a trace (the 20 H rule of EMC design guides; band 10 H to 100 H; no verified citation)

continuous_bound.note: upper bound on any line of any two-level waveform with this swing and edge; loose by construction

pattern_lines.window: the strongest line within one octave centred on the resonance, per named pattern; no pattern bounds the others

notes: screening evidence: ranks likely noise sources, never establishes EMC qualification

validated: the closed forms, the circuit solver and the receiver emulation against hand calculations and analytic cases (unit tests); not validated: no estimate has been correlated with a measurement, so no accuracy, confidence interval or bound is claimed; margins are screening margins, not pass or fail

uncertainty is reported as three separate things per estimate: numerical sensitivity (null for closed forms), parameter bands from rule-of-thumb defaults (band_db), and the named mechanisms not modelled (not_modelled)
common-mode radiation is a relative coupling-risk score (ranking only): it has no distance, no field value and no margin, and is never compared with an emission limit
hot-loop geometry is the traced copper path where routed copper joins the loop pads (traced_copper, partially_traced) and the pad-centre polygon elsewhere (placement_estimate)

differential-mode loop field is free space; in the current_limit scenario the radiated sweep is the upper envelope of the trapezoid, in the declared_operating_point scenario it is the harmonic lines of the ramp-on-pedestal switch current; peak against quasi-peak limits
limit tables are transcribed from the published numbers and must be verified against the standards
